subject: Migration mode selection: hosted vs dedicated vs private - Aurora Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: 
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: migration mode discussion + next steps

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the call today  great context on Aurora Health's latency and cost pain points. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Current primary inference: OpenAI-hosted API for chat + a legacy on-prem GPU cluster used for high-sensitivity workloads.
- Drivers for change: unpredictable latency at peak, rising per-token spend, and tighter data residency requirements for certain PHI-adjacent flows.
- Goals: predictable SLAs, cost predictability, and an easy migration path with minimal service disruption.

Deployment mode considerations (high level)
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, no ops, good for most conversational flows that don't require tenant-dedicated isolation.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools (predictable throughput), good trade-off for teams that need predictable cost and throughput but still want Redwood-managed infra.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): required if you need customer-managed networking or strict data residency / on-prem processing; more ops but gives full control.

Suggested next steps
1) Can you send a 1-page workload profile (peak QPS, average seq length, tokens per request, % of PII/PHI)?
2) I'll loop in our SE (Rishi) for a short technical scoping call  propose Mon/Tue next week.
3) I'll attach a short product brief and our Dedicated sizing template to help you fill the workload details.

Attachments: redwood-product-brief.pdf, redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (attached)

If you prefer an initial Dedicated vs Private cost comparison, let me know and I can include ballpark pricing in the follow-up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi Emma  thanks for the profile. A few technical clarifying questions to help us size Dedicated and scope any Private work: 

1) Token distribution: can you share a histogram or percentiles (p50/p90/p99) of token length per request? You referenced average ~350 but peaks to ~1800  we'd like the p90/p99 to size KV cache and KV memory.
2) Model variants: which models are you using on OpenAI today (gpt-4o/gpt-4/other)? Are you open to quantized variants we can validate for backend batch jobs?
3) Latency SLOs: what is the 95th percentile SLA you need for interactive chat flows?
4) Nightly batch jobs: are those latency-sensitive, or can they be scheduled into lower-priority Dedicated pools?

Migration approach notes (from SE perspective)
- Recommended phased plan: 1) Pilot on Hosted API for non-PHI chat flows (validate latency/cost), 2) Move high-volume interactive flows to Dedicated with reserved capacity and autoscale for peak, 3) For PHI flows, evaluate Private VPC deployment for isolation or keep on-prem with secure routing.
- Canary strategy: route 5-10% of production traffic to Redwood endpoints and compare latency/cost for 2 weeks before wider rollout.
- Data ingress: for Private we typically validate networking through a short proof-of-concept (VPN or VPC peering).

If you can share the token-percentile numbers and a sample of 100 anonymized request traces (latency + tokens), I can run a quick sizing and come back with a Dedicated configuration and a rough monthly cost estimate.

Happy to do Tue May 4 09:00 PST a I11 send a calendar invite with a short agenda.

Thanks,
